$comment: Rule catalog — the pipeline and the terminal decision. Standards 1, 2, 20.

rules.title: Every decision traverses the pipeline
rules.description: Every decision passes through each stage — offered odds, implied probability, vig removal, fair probability, uncertainty, edge, expected value, bankroll impact, exposure and correlation — and terminates in exactly BET or PASS, recorded before the event begins.
rules.rationale: The stages are ordered because each one consumes the last. Skipping one does not leave a gap; it leaves a number computed from something other than what it claims, and the result still looks like a complete answer.
rules.remediation: Record every stage value. If a stage genuinely does not apply, say so explicitly rather than omitting it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance that every stage is present and consistent with its inputs.

rules.title: PASS is recorded and counted as a successful decision
rules.description: A PASS is a first-class outcome of the pipeline, recorded with its reasons, and no metric treats declining a wager as a failure or a missed opportunity.
rules.rationale: If PASS is scored as inaction, every threshold in the pack becomes an obstacle to work around rather than a decision to respect. Most edges do not clear the bar, so most decisions should be PASSes, and a process producing them is functioning rather than idle.
rules.remediation: Record PASSes with their reasons and remove any metric that penalises them.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that PASSes are recorded with reasons matching the gates that actually failed. Whether the surrounding culture treats a PASS as a success is not something a record can show.

rules.title: No wager is recommended without considering the offered price
rules.description: No wager is recommended, suggested, or placed without the offered price entering the decision. A recommendation with no price attached is void, not merely weak.
rules.rationale: Without a price there is no edge, no expected value, and nothing to decide — only an opinion about who will win. The price is not one input among several; it is the input that makes the others mean anything.
rules.remediation: Obtain the price, run the pipeline, and record the decision. If no price is available, there is no decision to make.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that a price is present in every recorded decision. A recommendation made outside the ledger — in conversation, a message, a spreadsheet — is not visible to this check.

rules.title: A wager's quality is never judged by its result
rules.description: A winning wager is never treated as proof it was a good bet, and a losing wager is never treated as proof it was a bad one. Bet quality is judged from the information available at decision time. Both directions are one behaviour and one rule.
rules.rationale: This is the invariant the whole pack is built around. Judging decisions by outcomes teaches the wrong lesson from every result: a lucky win reinforces a process that will lose over time, and an unlucky loss discards one that would have won. Over a career the error compounds in the direction of abandoning discipline exactly when it is working.
rules.remediation: Review the decision against what was known when it was made. If the process was sound, a loss changes nothing about it.
rules.$assuranceNote: NOT MECHANICALLY EVALUATED. This prohibits a way of reasoning, and reasoning is not in the record. What the structure CAN do is make the violation harder: results live outside the digested decision block, so nothing about a decision changes when its outcome arrives. That is a structural defence, not a detection. This rule reports not-evaluated unless a human attests to it.

rules.title: No wager is recommended merely to create action
rules.description: No wager is placed or recommended because a wager was wanted — because the game is on, because nothing has been bet today, or because passing feels like doing nothing.
rules.rationale: An action bet is a wager placed for the feeling of having one, and the feeling does not care about the price. It is the mechanism by which a disciplined process quietly becomes an undisciplined one, because every individual action bet looks small.
rules.remediation: Record the PASS. Having no position is a position.
rules.$assuranceNote: NOT MECHANICALLY EVALUATED. An action bet that clears every threshold is indistinguishable in the record from a considered one, because the difference is why it was taken. This reports not-evaluated unless attested.

rules.title: No betting quota is imposed
rules.description: No target, minimum, or expected number of wagers per day, week, or season is set, whether in configuration, in a plan, or as an informal expectation. A period with no wagers is a valid outcome.
rules.rationale: A quota inverts the decision: instead of the edge deciding whether to bet, the calendar does, and the thresholds become obstacles between the bettor and a number they have promised themselves. Every quota is eventually met by lowering the bar.
rules.remediation: Remove the quota. Count PASSes as decisions in whatever reporting replaced it.
rules.$assuranceNote: A declared quota in configuration is detectable. An informal expectation — a habit, a target someone holds in their head, a report that counts only wagers placed — is not, and is the far more common form.
